narrative.overview:
Modern, sleek, minimalist: generous whitespace, few borders, flat surfaces, no unnecessary shadows or gradients. Warm but professional — the yellow/brown palette feels approachable without tipping into playful, because this is still a tool handling HR, performance and financial data. Clarity over decoration: managers need to scan and act fast, so brand color is used purposefully on accents, CTAs and active states rather than everywhere.

Two palettes share one token set. The marketing site and auth pages keep the warm cream/brown identity; the authenticated dashboard swaps in a yellow/white/black theme via a `.dashboard-theme` class on the app shell rather than by touching `:root`. Every token name is identical between them, so no component knows which palette it is rendering in. The public applicant surface extends that same move a third time with a `--file-*` set scoped to its own layout root and tinted at runtime by the company's brand color.

Status lives in its own palette and never borrows brand yellow or brown, so a brand accent can never be mistaken for an alert.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white ground (#FFFBF2), not stark white
Flat surfaces separated by 1px warm borders, shadow-sm at most
One typeface (Inter) at a fixed six-step scale from 32px down to 12px
Brand yellow reserved for the single primary action and active state
A separate status palette with darkened text hues that clear AA

rules.name: The Surface-Root Scoping Rule
rules.body: A palette that only one surface needs is declared on that surface's own layout root, never on :root. The dashboard does this with the .dashboard-theme class; the applicant surface does it with a --file-* custom-property set as an inline style on its layout. Either way the global tokens stay untouched, and nothing outside the scope can inherit a value meant for one page.

rules.name: The Muted-Ink Floor Rule
rules.body: On the cream ground, text-secondary (#8A7A66) measures ~4.2:1 and misses the AA floor. Secondary text on cream uses brand-brown-soft (#7A6653, ~5.3:1) instead.

rules.name: The Computed Foreground Rule
rules.body: When a color enters the product at runtime — an owner picking a brand color from a plain color input, with no contrast check attached — the foreground on it is computed, never assumed. readableTextOn() takes WCAG relative luminance and returns #2E2317 or #FFFFFF, so a dark brand and a pale brand both land readable.

rules.name: The Status Separation Rule
rules.body: Brand yellow/brown is never reused to signal status. This avoids ambiguity between 'this is a brand accent' and 'this needs your attention.'

rules.name: The Shared Pill Rule
rules.body: One shared pill owns the markup — surface-muted fill, full radius, 12px medium label in a darkened *-text token, a 6px dot in the matching fill hue — and each module declares its own vocabulary as a PillStyle map beside its feature. A new status set inherits the shape and the contrast floor; it never re-invents them.

dos: Do scope a one-surface palette to that surface's layout root, the way .dashboard-theme and --file-* both do, and keep :root for the shared world.
Do compute the foreground on any color the product did not choose at build time.
Do size controls to their content class rather than to the column — 13rem for a date, 34rem for a short answer.
Do separate sections with a 1px warm rule and vertical rhythm rather than by wrapping each one in a card.
Do dock a chosen file as a named row with its size and a remove control.
Do pair every status color with a text label, and use the darkened *-text tokens for that label.
donts: Don't introduce a second palette on a public surface. Everything but the company accent is the marketing/auth palette under a local name.

Don't place a small muted label directly above a heading as a kicker or eyebrow. Where the company's name has to appear above the role title, it sits on its own ruled letterhead band, separated by a rule.
Don't paint status color or brand yellow onto the applicant surface. The company's accent is the only accent.
Don't use a drop shadow for emphasis; surfaces are flat and separated by a warm 1px border.
Don't ship the browser's own file-input chrome, or a dashed drop-zone rectangle, in place of a drawn control.
Don't put status text directly on a solid brand-yellow fill — it lands near 3.5:1. Status stays on white or surface-muted.
